content.jointProblem: Can the existing site data plus a newly designed groundwater monitoring network resolve the leachate flow direction, its seasonal variation and the lateral extent of the COD plume beneath the temporary storage yard, and support a containment and treatment proposal the Subotica Environmental Inspectorate will accept? The first experiment would test whether lowland alluvial monitoring and flow/transport modelling methods developed at bank-filtration and recharge sites transfer to a waste-yard leachate setting.

rationale.text: The researcher has directly relevant consulting experience in site characterisation and monitoring network design for a regional water utility.

sources.quote: advising on site characterisation methodology and monitoring network design

rationale.text: He has built and operated dense multi-level piezometer networks to characterise hydraulic gradients and vertical exchange fluxes, which is the core instrumentation this task requires.

sources.quote: a network of 18 multi-level piezometers installed at three transects perpendicular to the riverbank
monitoring network installation and data collection at two BF sites on the Danube and two recharge transects in Vojvodina

rationale.text: He has constructed and calibrated groundwater flow models and used particle-tracking transport simulation to estimate travel times, which is the basis for predicting where leachate moves.

sources.quote: MT3DMS particle tracking indicated median travel times of 18–42 days at the production well field

rationale.text: His synthesis work explicitly addresses method selection for data-sparse lowland settings, which matches a site with only a 1993 hydrogeological sketch.

sources.quote: reviews methods applicable in data-sparse lowland settings (slug tests, streambed temperature profiling, environmental tracers, water balance approaches)

rationale.text: He has worked on groundwater vulnerability assessment recalibrated against local contamination data, which is directly analogous to a monitoring network built around a known contamination source.

sources.quote: applied the DRASTIC vulnerability indexing method recalibrated against local contamination data

rationale.text: His stated preferences and openness align with the task: he wants field measurement work and is open to contract research on site-specific hydrogeological assessment.

sources.quote: Prefers projects with a clear field measurement component rather than purely modelling-focused work.
contract research on site-specific hydrogeological assessment or recharge studies

constraints.text: The work is deadline-bound: four groundwater monitoring wells must be installed and a remediation proposal submitted within 120 days, by late June 2024.

sources.quote: issued an order requiring us to install four groundwater monitoring wells within 120 days and to submit a remediation proposal

constraints.text: Baseline data are almost absent: only a 1993 hydrogeological sketch exists, and neither the flow direction nor the contamination extent is known, so new field characterisation is unavoidable.

sources.quote: We have a hydrogeological sketch from when the site was first permitted in 1993 but nothing more recent.
We do not know how far the contamination has moved or which direction groundwater flows under the site at different seasons.

constraints.text: The output must be acceptable to the regulator, so the plan has to be framed as a leachate containment and treatment proposal, not only a monitoring exercise.

sources.quote: draft a leachate containment and treatment proposal that the inspectorate will accept

constraints.text: The measured COD is already well above the threshold that triggers a formal response, so containment and treatment options must be part of the scope from the start.

sources.quote: COD came back at 3,400 mg/L, which is well above the threshold that triggers a formal response

constraints.text: The company has no dedicated research budget and only a basic wet-chemistry bench, so laboratory analyses beyond routine COD/heavy-metal sampling must be planned with external capacity.

sources.quote: we have no dedicated research budget or laboratory beyond the basic wet-chemistry bench used for leachate monitoring

risks: Transfer gap: the researcher's documented field sites are riverbank bank-filtration sites, agricultural recharge transects and canal systems; there is no evidence in his material of work on landfill or waste-yard leachate, so the method transfer must be tested in the first field campaign rather than assumed.

Transport modelling evidence is limited to particle tracking of travel times at a production well field, not reactive or attenuating contaminant transport; predicting COD and leachate behaviour in the subsurface is unproven for this team and site.

With only a 1993 hydrogeological sketch and unknown seasonal flow direction, the four wells could be sited off-plume; a preliminary reconnaissance and seasonal head measurement are needed before final siting.

The 120-day window leaves little room for drilling permits, contractor procurement and well installation, and the company's lack of a dedicated research budget makes the field and laboratory work vulnerable to funding delays.

The researcher's availability within the spring 2024 window is unknown, and his stated capacity for industrial PhD co-supervision starts only in autumn 2026, so an industrial PhD format cannot serve this deadline.
COD values were produced on the company's in-house bench; the inspectorate may require accredited laboratory analyses, which is not evidenced anywhere in the material.
questions: Is the researcher available to start field work within the 120-day window (spring 2024), given that his availability is currently unknown?
Would he prefer a joint project or is he also willing to co-supervise an industrial PhD student, given that his industrial PhD supervision willingness is recorded as unknown?
Who will carry out and fund the drilling and installation of the four wells, and which permits are required for drilling on the site?
What site information exists beyond the 1993 sketch: depth to water table, liner construction details, existing boreholes, and any nearby production or monitoring wells?
Which parameters and analytical standards will the Subotica Environmental Inspectorate require, and is an accredited laboratory available for confirmatory analyses?
What waste types and volumes were stored in the yard over the twelve years, and were any hazardous items present that would change the leachate composition?
